children: Hilton’s India growth is increasingly being shaped by development partnerships that allow its brands to reach new markets, price points and traveller segments while creating scalable models for owners and developers

Hilton’s India strategy is entering a new phase, moving beyond its established presence in major business markets towards a broader network spanning emerging cities, leisure destinations and the mid-market. The model is increasingly built around partnerships, with Hilton combining its brands, operating expertise, distribution and loyalty ecosystem with local developers and hospitality companies to accelerate expansion.

That makes the perspective of Zubin Saxena, Sr. Vice President & Regional Head, South Asia, Hilton, particularly relevant to the owners, developers and investors attending the Indian Hospitality Summit & Awards 2026 at JW Marriott New Delhi Aerocity.

Hilton’s recent India expansion has been driven by strategic agreements that place development capital and execution with local partners while bringing Hilton’s brands and commercial infrastructure to the properties. In April 2026, Hilton and Olive Hospitality signed the first 10 Spark by Hilton hotel signings in India, under a broader agreement to sign and open 150 franchised properties across the country.

Hilton has also signed agreements with NILE Hospitality for 75 Hampton by Hilton hotels and with Royal Orchid Hotels for another 125 Hampton hotels. Together with its existing pipeline, these agreements put Hilton on track to exceed 400 trading hotels in India in the coming years.
Taking international brands beyond the metros

The partnership strategy is also widening Hilton’s addressable market. Spark by Hilton made its Asia Pacific debut in June 2026 with openings in Bengaluru and Goa, while additional signings span Jaipur, Nashik, Mathura, Pune, Rajkot and Hyderabad. Hampton’s expansion is similarly aimed at emerging markets, with its first Indian hotels under the NILE agreement planned across Gujarat, Rajasthan, Punjab and Bihar.

The model is not limited to mid-market growth. Hilton continues to expand its premium and luxury presence, including Waldorf Astoria Jaipur and the India debut of LXR Hotels & Resorts with The Den Bengaluru. Its portfolio therefore gives development partners access to different segments without requiring a single brand proposition to fit every market.
Building scale with owner economics in mind

The approach sits within Hilton’s wider asset-light growth model. Globally, Hilton had more than 9,400 properties and nearly 1.4 million rooms across 144 countries and territories as of its second-quarter 2026 reporting, with 541,300 rooms in its development pipeline at June 30, 2026.

For India, the next phase is therefore as much about building the right partnerships as adding hotels. The proposition for owners is access to global brands, distribution, Hilton Honors and operating capabilities, while Hilton gains a scalable route into markets where branded hospitality supply is still developing. The partnership itself becomes a growth engine.
